lines.trans: Do you have any idea what you are saying right now?
Of course I do. I have come to love him deeply as a human being.
You do not understand anything about love yet.
Is having a child with a married man what love means?
Don't talk back so insolently to your mother!
Until you were born, that man loved me.

words.gram: Plain imperative of くれる (give/do for me).

lines.trans: Yet the moment you were born, he drifted away from me.
Did you resent me all this time? Is that why you kept tying me down?
Because as long as I had you, my connection to him would continue.
Being a woman mattered more to both of us than being mother and daughter.
I wished I could have eaten more of your home cooking, Mom.
Goodbye, Mom.

meanings.note: Reflexive pronoun pointing back to the person under discussion.

examples.text: 自分の言葉で話します。
examples.trans: I speak in my own words.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
分かってる asks or states ongoing understanding; plain past 分かった means 'got it! / I understand'.

examples.text: 日本語が少し分かります。

examples.trans: Got it, I will come right away.

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Confident everyday word that works either before a predicate or as a standalone answer.

examples.text: もちろん手伝いますよ。

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Filler or polite attention-getter.

examples.text: あの、ちょっとよろしいですか。
examples.trans: Excuse me, do you have a moment?

examples.text: あの、実は相談があります。
examples.trans: Um, actually I have something to ask you.

meanings.en: respectful word for a person (かた)
meanings.note: Read かた, polite replacement for 人 (ひと) when announcing visitors or customers.

examples.text: あの方はどなたですか。

examples.trans: The person in charge has arrived.

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Refers to humans in general or human nature.

examples.text: 人間には表と裏がある。
examples.trans: Human beings have a public face and a hidden side.

meanings.note: Auxiliary godan verb following て-form.

examples.text: つい忘れてしまいました。
本を全部読んでしまった。
examples.trans: I finished reading the whole book.

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Adverb.

examples.text: まだ終わっていません。

meanings.note: Noun.
Colloquial quotative/emphatic particle expressing surprise or dismissal.

examples.text: そんなことなんて知らない。
examples.trans: I don't know anything like that.

examples.text: 嘘だなんて信じられない。
examples.trans: I can't believe it's a lie.

meanings.note: Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
Read ひと when standing as an independent noun.

examples.text: 親切な人に会いました。

meanings.note: Standard word for a child or kid.

examples.text: 公園で子供が遊んでいます。
examples.trans: Children are playing in the park.

examples.text: 子供のころ北海道に住んでいました。
examples.trans: When I was a child, I lived in Hokkaido.

examples.text: 奥さんがいる人の間に子供を産むことが愛なの？
examples.trans: Is having a child with a married man what love means?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').

examples.text: 子供が生意気言わないの！
examples.trans: Don't talk back so insolently to your mother!

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

meanings.en: nothing more than (after past verb); up to
meanings.note: After a plain verb + です (出店したまでです), modestly states 'we simply did that and nothing more'.

examples.text: 念のため聞いたまでです。
examples.trans: I merely asked just in case.

meanings.en: do a favor for the speaker
meanings.note: After a te-form (会ってくれる？), warmly asks 'will you do that for us?'

examples.trans: Will you come again for me?

examples.text: 母が料理を作ってくれました。
examples.trans: My mother cooked food for me.

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

examples.text: でもあなたが生まれたとたん、私から離れていった。
examples.trans: Yet the moment you were born, he drifted away from me.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。
私のことずっと憎かったの？だから縛り続けてきたの？
examples.trans: Did you resent me all this time? Is that why you kept tying me down?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

examples.text: 私のことずっと憎かったの？だから縛り続けてきたの？
examples.trans: Did you resent me all this time? Is that why you kept tying me down?

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: come; go do something and return (after て-form)
meanings.note: Written in kana after a て-form (話してきます), expresses stepping away to do an action and coming back.

examples.text: ちょっと水を買ってきます。
examples.trans: I will go buy some water and be right back.

meanings.note: Attaches to the irrealis (a-stem) of godan verbs.

examples.trans: I was called by the teacher.

meanings.note: Conditional particle attached to the hypothetical (e) stem of verbs and adjectives.

examples.text: 練習すれば上手になります。
examples.trans: If you practice, you will get better.
If it's cheap, I'll buy it.

examples.text: あなたさえいれば、彼との関係が続くから。
examples.trans: Because as long as I had you, my connection to him would continue.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: side or option in comparisons and advice (〜ほうがいい)
meanings.note: Paired with がいい after past or negative forms to recommend the better course ('it is better to...').

examples.text: 早く寝たほうがいいよ。
examples.trans: You had better go to sleep early.

examples.text: 傘を持ったほうがいいです。
examples.trans: It is better to bring an umbrella.

meanings.note: Everyday spoken counterpart of なぜ or どうして.

examples.text: なんで知っているんですか。

meanings.note: Intensifies the following adverb or verb, as in もっとちゃんと見て.

examples.text: もっと近くで見てください。
もっとゆっくり話してください。

meanings.note: Ichidan verb; causative 食べさせる can mean 'to feed/support'.

examples.text: 朝ごはんを食べましたか。
家族を食べさせるために働く。
examples.trans: I work to support my family.

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.

なら.gloss: if it is; in the case of

meanings.note: Conditional topic marker placed right after a noun or pronoun (あなたなら 'if it were you').

examples.text: あなたならどうしますか？
examples.trans: If it were you, what would you do?

examples.text: 明日なら時間があります。
examples.trans: If it is tomorrow, I have time.

meanings.note: Standard polite 'goodbye'.
